chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), similar to it.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I asked him about the hand, so he said: Half the wergild, and regarding the ear, half the wergild when it is cut off from its root.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for the compensation of cutting off a hand or ear?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific valuation of bodily injuries within the Shia jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money), establishing that severing a hand or an ear from its root incurs half the full wergild. It reflects the systematic categorization of injuries found in *al-Kafi*, distinguishing between partial and complete compensation based on the extent of the damage. This ruling underscores the precision with which Shia scholars derived legal penalties from the Imams' teachings to ensure equitable restitution.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it’.

A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, 
‘I asked about the hand, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Half the wergild, and regarding the ears, half the wergild when these are cut off from its roots’.
